_readme: assets/js/grade-6-mini-games.js reads this file, draws one card per
game, and plays each one with the shared Game Zone engine.
Card fields:  slug, title, skill, blurb, facts, minutes, theme
Game fields:  id (used to remember stars), type, instructions, and
vocab-drop   pairs: [{ word, meaning, example? }], perRound?
adventure    intro?, scenes: [{ place, story, sentence (with ___),
sequence     stories: [{ title, clue?, sentences (in the RIGHT
order - the game shuffles them), after? }]
To add words, scenes or stories, add entries here and run build.cmd.
title: Grade 6 Mini-Games

games.title: Word Drop
games.blurb: Drag each word onto its meaning. Match it and you see the word used in a real sentence.
games.instructions: Drag a word onto its meaning - or tap the word, then tap the meaning.

pairs.meaning: very old; from a long time ago
pairs.example: Sigiriya is an ancient rock fortress.

pairs.meaning: ready to face danger without showing fear
pairs.example: The brave firefighter carried the kitten to safety.

pairs.meaning: wanting to know or learn about something
pairs.example: The curious boy asked the guide a hundred questions.
An elephant is an enormous animal.
Carry the glass vase carefully - it is fragile.

pairs.meaning: happy to give and share with others
pairs.example: Our generous neighbour shared her mangoes with the whole lane.

pairs.meaning: the time when crops are cut and gathered
pairs.example: The farmers celebrated after the paddy harvest.

pairs.meaning: a trip from one place to another
pairs.example: The train journey to Ella took seven hours.

pairs.meaning: not wide; with little space from side to side
pairs.example: The path up the mountain was steep and narrow.

pairs.meaning: to keep someone or something safe from harm
pairs.example: A helmet protects your head when you ride a bicycle.
After the heavy rain, the river became rapid and brown.

pairs.meaning: hard to find because there is not enough
pairs.example: Water becomes scarce in the dry season.
The timid deer ran back into the forest.
The sun vanished behind the dark clouds.

pairs.meaning: to walk around slowly, without a plan
pairs.example: We wandered along Galle Face Green in the evening.

pairs.meaning: a special time when people celebrate
pairs.example: Vesak is a festival of lanterns and lights.

pairs.meaning: dark, dull and a little sad
pairs.example: It was a gloomy, rainy afternoon.

games.title: The Lost Temple Bell
games.blurb: Help Nimal and Sita follow an old map. Choose the right word at every stop to move along the trail.
games.instructions: Read each part of the story, then choose the word that fits the gap.
games.intro: Nimal and his sister Sita love mysteries. One rainy afternoon, something in Grandfather's cupboard starts a real adventure.

scenes.story: Behind a pile of books, Sita notices a roll of yellow paper tied with string.
scenes.sentence: Inside the roll, the children find ___ old map.
scenes.tip: Say the next word aloud. Does 'old' begin with a vowel sound or a consonant sound?
scenes.explain: We use 'an' before a vowel sound: an old map, an egg, an umbrella.

scenes.story: The paper is thin and the ink has faded to brown.
scenes.sentence: The map ___ very old, and its edges are torn.
scenes.tip: 'The map' is one thing. Which verb goes with one thing?
scenes.explain: 'The map' is singular, so we use 'is'. We use 'are' with plurals: the maps are old.

scenes.story: Nimal and Sita want an adult to help them read the map.
scenes.sentence: Yesterday, they ___ the map to their teacher, Mr Perera.
scenes.tip: Look at the first word. 'Yesterday' tells you the action is already finished.
scenes.explain: 'Yesterday' shows the past, so we use the past tense: show becomes showed.

scenes.story: Mr Perera studies the map carefully and points to a tiny drawing of falling water.
scenes.sentence: "Look! There is a secret cave ___ the waterfall," he says.
scenes.tip: We need a word that tells us WHERE the cave is.
scenes.explain: 'Behind' is a preposition of place. 'During' and 'since' are about time.

scenes.story: On Saturday morning, the children get ready for the long walk.
scenes.sentence: They pack two ___: one for water and one for food.
scenes.tip: 'Two' means more than one. How do we show more than one bag?
scenes.explain: After 'two' we need a plural noun. Most nouns just add -s: one bag, two bags.

scenes.story: Soon the wide village road turns into a jungle track.
scenes.sentence: The jungle path is ___ than the village road.
scenes.tip: The sentence compares TWO things, and it uses the word 'than'.
scenes.explain: To compare two things we use the comparative form with 'than': narrow becomes narrower than.

scenes.story: Suddenly, the leaves shake and a branch cracks above them.
scenes.tip: 'Somebody' means one person, and the noise is happening right now.
scenes.explain: 'Somebody' is singular and the action is happening now, so we say 'Somebody is coming'. (It was only a friendly monkey!)

scenes.story: Nimal's legs ache after the long climb, but the cave is close now.
scenes.sentence: Nimal is tired, ___ he keeps walking.
scenes.tip: The two ideas are opposites: feeling tired, and still walking. Which word joins opposite ideas?
scenes.explain: 'But' joins two ideas that contrast: tired, but still walking.

scenes.story: Behind the curtain of water, the cave is dark and cool.
scenes.sentence: Inside the cave, ___ find a bronze bell covered in dust.
scenes.tip: We need a word for the people DOING the action - the subject of the sentence.
scenes.explain: 'They' is a subject pronoun: it does the action. 'Them' is an object pronoun, and 'their' shows belonging.

scenes.story: The children carry the heavy bell carefully back down the mountain.
scenes.sentence: The next day, the children ___ the bell to the museum, and everyone cheered.
scenes.tip: 'Cheered' tells you the story is in the past. Which form is the simple past?
scenes.explain: 'Take' is an irregular verb: take becomes took. ('Taken' needs a helper, as in 'have taken'.) You found the lost temple bell!

games.title: Story Scramble
games.blurb: The sentences of four short texts are mixed up. Drag them back into the right order.
games.instructions: Drag the sentences into the right order, or use the arrow buttons. Then press Check my order.

stories.title: The Thirsty Crow
stories.clue: Look for time words such as 'One hot day' and 'At last'.
sentences: One hot day, a crow was very thirsty.
He flew from place to place looking for water.
At last he found a pot with a little water at the bottom.
He dropped pebbles into the pot, one by one.
The water rose to the top, and the crow drank happily.
stories.after: Moral: where there is a will, there is a way.

stories.title: Sunil's Sports Day
stories.clue: Follow the day from morning to afternoon.
sentences: On Friday morning, Sunil woke up early and put on his house T-shirt.
At school, the teacher called the runners to the starting line.
When the whistle blew, Sunil ran as fast as he could.
He crossed the finishing line just before his friend Kavin.
In the afternoon, the principal gave him a gold medal.
stories.after: Words like 'On Friday morning', 'When' and 'In the afternoon' show the reader the order of events.

stories.title: How to Plant a Seed
stories.clue: Instructions use order words: First, Next, Then, After that, Finally.
sentences: First, fill a small pot with soil.
Next, make a hole in the soil with your finger.
Then, put the seed in the hole and cover it.
After that, water the soil gently.
Finally, keep the pot in a sunny place and watch it grow.
stories.after: Order words make instructions easy to follow. Try using them in your own writing.

stories.title: The Lion and the Mouse
stories.clue: Think about cause and effect: each event makes the next one happen.
sentences: A lion was sleeping under a tree when a little mouse ran across his nose.
The angry lion caught the mouse, but she begged him to let her go.
The lion laughed and set the tiny mouse free.
A few days later, the lion was trapped in a hunter's net.
The mouse heard him roar and chewed through the ropes to save him.
stories.after: Moral: even the smallest friend can be a great help.
